author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A piece of Concord Public Library history has come home after 48,220 days: a bound magazine checked out in 1894 and returned this month by a Barrington resident who had kept it on a bookshelf for decades.

John Hanson told the Concord Monitor he did not know how the volume entered his family’s possession. The item is the September 1894 issue of “The Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine,” still bearing the library’s markings and a one-week lending notice.

Hanson decided to return it after reading that the library had started a year-long freeze on overdue fines. By the Monitor’s calculation, the periodical would have accumulated $12,055 in penalties under a daily fine, although the library would not have charged him. Staff verified the date, issue number and bookplate to confirm that the copy had not simply been removed from circulation.

The library does not plan to lend the fragile magazine again. Instead, archivists hope to display it in the Concord Room, which houses local historical material. The episode gives the fine-free initiative an unusually tangible result and leaves staff with a mystery: who borrowed the magazine more than a century ago, and how it traveled from Concord to Hanson’s shelves.
dek: A Barrington man returned an 1894 magazine after spotting the library’s year-long fine freeze; archivists hope to display it in the Concord Room.
headline: Concord library receives book overdue by more than 132 years
